novel_mechanics_found: vc33 is a FLUID-PUMP puzzle (the registry called it support-clearance; the fluid model makes it legible). Black cells are fluid; colored pieces FLOAT on a fluid surface with their 2px bar riding the surface and a triangular cap trailing; 9-5-9 support feet at the field edge are directional PUMPS: clicking a 9-pad pulls exactly one quantum (2px on L3, 3px on L4/L5) of fluid toward that side; pumps refuse when a pocket hits its wall-top capacity. Pieces win by aligning their bar with the same-colored 1px/2px door segment embedded in a wall (L3: all three pieces bar==door row simultaneously -> instant win; L4: single piece bar==door rows -> instant win on the aligning pump click). L4/L5 add TRANSIT DOORS: long color-1 window segments in walls OPEN (turn color-12) when BOTH adjacent pockets surfaces sit exactly at the window sill (last-2-cells along gravity); CLICKING the open door makes adjacent floating pieces cross the wall -- and if pieces flank the door on BOTH sides, they SWAP simultaneously. L5 rotates the whole physics 90 degrees (gravity rightward, pumps on the right edge -- retroactively explaining why L1/L2 controls were edge clicks at x=1/x=61). L5 also introduced a ONE-WAY pump (wall2 middle-side pull is a check valve that never fires), making the fluid economy directional. The 7-colored top row is a WASTED-CLICK budget: only no-op clicks burn it, and exhausting it is GAME OVER (empty terminal frame, levels_completed resets to 0) -- NOT a level restart.
narrative: Replayed the banked 10-click prefix to L2. L3 (three pieces, three doors, four pumps): derived the fluid-conservation ledger live; the exact-fit design (every pocket ends empty) disambiguated bar-alignment as the win rule; won at step 41. L4 (single piece, two transit windows, one colored door): discovered window-sill opening, door-click crossing, and won by floating the piece across two pockets to its door at step 66; gate-verified the 66-label line (reproduced=True at claimed_level=4). L5 (rotated physics, two pieces with crossing paths, a check-valve pump): reverse-engineered the full economy and proved by unit-conservation that BOTH nominal targets (each piece bar==same-color door with required surfaces) are unreachable -- the one-way valve caps the middle pocket one 3px-quantum short. Tested the piece-swap trick at the shared wall (works mechanically), alignment from both sides of each door, and a crossed-target configuration (E on the B slot from the top pocket + B on the E slot from the bottom pocket, both exact) -- none fired the predicate. Exhausted the wasted-click budget deliberately expecting a level restart and discovered it is GAME OVER instead. Stopped at 414/500 env steps with L4 verified; L5 win rule remains undiscovered.
gotchas: Click labels use nested data coords: {"action":6,"data":{"x":..,"y":..}}.

The 7-row at the top burns ONLY on wasted/no-op clicks; effective pump/door clicks are free. Exhausting it is GAME OVER (empty frame, level resets to 0), not a level restart -- never burn it deliberately.
Pump quantum is level-specific: 2px per click on L3, 3px on L4/L5.
Pumps refuse silently (sometimes without even burning the 7-bar) when: source pocket empty, destination at wall-top capacity, or the pump is a designed one-way check valve (L5 wall2 middle-side).

Transit windows (color-1 wall segments) open only when BOTH pocket surfaces sit exactly at the sill (the last 2 cells of the window along the gravity direction); the open door renders color-12 with 1px fluid channels flanking the wall.
Clicking an open door crosses ALL sill-adjacent floating pieces: with pieces on both sides they swap places -- exploitable as a maneuver, unavoidable as a hazard.

L3 win = all pieces bar==door simultaneously; L4 win fired instantly on the pump click that aligned the single piece; L5: bar==door alignment (same-color, either side, and crossed-color) did NOT win -- the L5 predicate is still unknown. Next attempt: consider that L5 may require pieces to CROSS their colored doors (needs both-side sills at the door columns, which demands more fluid than one pocket chain holds -- maybe via an unexplored source), or that the B piece must stay strictly on its own fluid column.
L5 economy: total fluid = 31 quanta; the check valve makes M-pocket max 13; bar c20-21 in M (surface 22 = 14 quanta) is provably unreachable -- do not re-derive this.
